children: Turkey's finance minister Mehmet Simsek said on Sunday he would meet index compiler MSCI's senior management and global investors next month to discuss reforms and address concerns about Turkey's capital markets and investment environment.

Speaking in an interview with broadcaster Kanal 7, Simsek said he expected concrete reforms and the government's structural policy efforts on the financial markets to have taken shape by then. Here are some details:
Simsek called MSCI's statement reasonable and constructive.
Simsek will meet with MSCI's senior management and discuss steps already taken and future steps by authorities, Simsek said.
Simsek said the liquidation of funds was proceeding as planned and faster than previously anticipated.
As part of the fund liquidation process, a total of 161 billion lira ($3.20 billion) has been paid to investors with savings in funds that are ordered to be liquidated.
Corporate bonds linked to funds in liquidation total 55.2 billion lira, of a 1 trillion lira market.
Simsek said new legislation will raise penalties, particularly for manipulation through coordinated trades.
The Capital Markets Board's retrospective review of manipulated stocks and transactions will be largely completed by the end of this month, Simsek said.
Simsek said the government does not plan to continue the sliding-scale fuel tax system next year, assuming that the Iran war will end.
